title: Percentile-SLO-based Rollouts and Rollback Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build an orchestrator and control-plane primitives for percentile-SLO-driven progressive rollouts. The goal is a reusable service that coordinates: canary deployments, automated % traffic ramps, SLO-aware health checks (p50/p90/p99), feature-flag integration, and programmatic rollbacks when regressions are detected. This is not a replacement for our canary APIs, but an opinionated layer that implements safe default ramps and failure modes used by hosted and dedicated clusters.

Why this work: 
- Current rollouts rely on ad-hoc ramps and manual decisions, causing longer incident response and inconsistent risk profiles across services.
- We need a standard way to express ‘acceptable degradation’ using percentile SLOs (rather than just error rate or simple latency means).
- Automating rollback reduces time-to-remediate and prevents prolonged customer impact when a bad model/serving change slips through.

Goals and success criteria:
- Implement a rollout controller that supports: initial canary (N%) -> staged ramps (N -> M -> 100%) -> automated rollback triggers.
- Health checks evaluate multiple signals: p99 latency, tail-token-generation time, error rate, and sample-quality signals from eval hooks.
- Rollback decision uses configurable heuristics (e.g., p99 > baseline * 1.25 for 3 consecutive windows OR error rate spike > 2x baseline).
- Expose control knobs in Console: ramp schedule, safety window, rollback sensitivity, opt-in dry-run mode.
- Integrate with feature flags (FF) SDK to gate new model variants per-org and per-route.
- Add observability: per-step metrics, alerting rules, and a rollout audit trail for postmortems.
- Document migration steps and runbook for on-call.

Design notes and choices:
- SLOs used: p50, p90, p99 latency (token and response), error-rate, and a composite quality score (from our existing eval pipelines). Prioritize p99 for rollback decisions but keep error-rate as a fast-fail signal.
- Use rolling window aggregation (1m windows, 3-window majority) to avoid noisy single-window rollbacks.
- Percent-based ramping: typical preset = [1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%] with safety windows configurable per-environment. Customers and enterprise tenants can override sequences.
- Safety net: if the orchestrator loses connectivity to metrics backend, pause ramps and revert to the last known safe state.
- Feature flags are the mechanism for traffic slicing. The orchestrator will call FF API to change percentage rules atomically.
- Implement an opt-in simulated rollout mode where decisions are logged but not applied — useful for validating thresholds against historical traffic.

Operational considerations:
- Metrics ingestion: rely on Console’s per-route token and latency metrics. Add sampling hooks for model-quality signals (small sample of generated outputs to eval service).
- Audit: every ramp and rollback must generate an immutable entry with reason, metric diffs, and links to traces/PR.
- Safety overrides: on-call can pause/resume or force-rollforward/rollback. Manual approval step required for >50% ramps in certain org tiers.

Testing and migration plan:
- Unit tests for decision logic with synthetic metric traces.
- Integration tests in staging: run 10 simulated rollouts against real metric streams in the canary cluster.
- Gradual rollout of orchestrator itself: start as a user-configured job in staging, then enable as default for non-critical routes, then expand to core runtime routes.

Open questions:
- How to incorporate model-quality signals at scale without spamming eval infra? Proposed: sample 0.1% of requests for quality scoring and prioritise on routes flagged as high-risk.
- Should enterprise customers have a separate rollback sensitivity profile? (PM suggests yes).

Acceptance criteria:
- Orchestrator deployed to staging and used for at least two non-prod rollouts with automated rollbacks triggered appropriately in simulation mode.
- Console UI surfaces rollout timeline and a per-step metric diff view.
- On-call runbook updated and playbook practiced in one live exercise.
